???+ remember "Before you start, remember"

    ??? question "What is occupancy, and does maximizing it always raise a kernel's throughput?"

        The number of active warps on an SM divided by the most it can hold, set by the tightest of its warp and block slots, registers and shared memory. No: a kernel can reach full throughput at low occupancy through instruction-level parallelism, which often makes it faster.

        Introduced in [B. Performance: G5. Occupancy and latency hiding](g5-occupancy.md).

    ??? question "What does one warp-wide load cost in global memory?"

        The number of distinct aligned 32-byte sectors that the warp's 32 addresses touch, not the number of bytes any one lane asked for.

        Introduced in [B. Performance: G4. Memory performance: coalescing and bank conflicts](g4-memory-performance.md).

    ??? question "What happens when a thread needs more live values than the registers it has been given?"

        The compiler spills some of them to local memory, which despite its name is a private slice of slow device memory, not on-chip storage.

        Introduced in [A. The machine: G3. The GPU memory hierarchy](g3-memory-hierarchy.md).
